name: Secure Payment Confirmation
plain: Authenticates a card payment with a passkey inside the browser.
meaning: Binds a WebAuthn credential to a payment so banks can confirm the person approved this exact amount.

web.api: PaymentRequest with method secure-payment-confirmation, securePaymentConfirmationAvailability, getSecurePaymentConfirmationCapabilities

access.prompt_ui: Browser sheet showing merchant and amount; needs passkey
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Authenticates a card payment with a passkey inside the browser.

limits.headline: Can confirm a card payment with a passkey that you approve in the browser
limits.user_action: You tap Pay, then confirm with your fingerprint, face or device PIN.
can: Show the shop name and amount before you confirm
Check you with a passkey that your bank set up
Send the bank proof that you approved this payment
cannot: Work before you set up a passkey with your bank
Work in Safari, Firefox or on iPhone
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support it. Safari and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: Confirm a card payment with a passkey or fingerprint, right in the browser.

marketing.name: Secure Payment Confirmation
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say it lets banks confirm a card payment with a passkey, with a consistent, secure pay sheet.

story.for_you: At checkout, a sheet shows the shop and amount and asks for your fingerprint or face. It replaces text message codes you have to type.
story.for_makers: Banks and card networks want it because it makes card fraud harder and cuts abandoned checkouts. It is part of the 3D Secure rules for online card payments.

use_cases.example: A bank confirms an online card payment with your fingerprint instead of an SMS code.
A retailer sees fewer failed checkouts because people no longer wait for a code.
An airline confirms a high value booking with a passkey.
Fraud teams get a cryptographic proof that the real card owner approved.
A card network lets a bank run its own check with no redirect.
A game store confirms a large purchase with your face.
